newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-East Midlands saga enlivens sector.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-East Midlands saga enlivens sector.

text.p: Britain's independent electricity companies were back in the spotlight on Thursday after East Midlands Electricity Plc said it would reject any takeover from U.S. group Dominion Resources at a price near 608p.

Dominion revealed it was mulling an offer for East Midlands late on Wednesday after shares in the electricity company had surged 70 pence to close at 607-1/2 pence, lifting the Nottingham-based group's value to more than 1.2 billion pounds ($1.97 billion).

However, shares in the independent electricity suppliers lost ground on the London stock market on Thursday, in stark contrast to active business on Wednesday when bid rumours helped the sector power ahead.

Dominion, an energy group which owns the power generator and distributor Virginia Power, said on Wednesday that it had been evaluating a potential offer for East Midlands "at a price not much in excess of 608p per share."

East Midlands responded on Thursday by saying that it would "reject an offer at that level, which it believes would undervalue East Midlands Electricity's prospects under its existing management team."
"At this level, our clear advice to shareholders would be to reject such an offer," said chairman of East Midlands Nigel Rudd.
Shares in East Midlands had tumbled 24 pence to 583-1/2 pence by 1339 GMT following the announcement.
City analysts also said an offer of 608 pence was too low.

"I'd say Dominion will be unsuccessful anywhere near six pounds. If you look at the precedent of other successful offers, you'd have to say that this one would have to come in north of eight pounds," said David Campbell, an analyst at Greig Middleton.

Speculation surrounding Britain's regional electricity companies (RECs) heated up last week after a unit controlled by U.S.-based CalEnergy launched a hostile 650 million pound bid for Northern Electric Plc.
CE Electric, the CalEnergy Co Inc unit bidding for Northern, raised its stake in Northern to 19.9 percent on Thursday after buying 6.5 million shares in the market.
CE bought the shares at its bid price of 630p per share, broker Hoare Govett said in a stock market disclosure statement.
Northern Electric's shares fell 5.5 pence to 625 in heavy trade by 1230 GMT, as rival "white knight" bidders failed to emerge to counter CE's hostile bid.
Out of the 12 privatised cash-rich RECS, seven have already changed ownership.

Shares in the other independent RECs surrendered recent gains as seen in Yorkshire Electricity Group Plc down 16 pence to 738, Southern Electric Plc off 2-1/2 pence to 666-1/2 and London Electricity Plc 13 pence lower at 604-1/2.
